info.name: JobLoom — Unauthenticated File Upload Test
info.description:
Tests ONE thing: can `POST /api/upload` store a file without any authentication?

The verdict is decided by the real server response, not by assumptions.

## Verified against current source
| Item | Confirmed value | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Endpoint | `POST /api/upload` | `src/server.js:68` mounts `uploadRoute` at `/api/upload`; `src/routes/upload.route.js:111` defines `router.post('/')` |
| Auth on POST | **none** — no `protect`, no role middleware | `src/routes/upload.route.js:111` |
| Auth on sibling GET | `protect` IS applied | `src/routes/upload.route.js:64` (`GET /signed-url`) |
| File field name | `file` (required) | `cloudUpload.single('file')` |
| `folder` field | optional text field; defaults to `jobloom_uploads` | `upload.route.js:116` → `upload.service.js:24` |
| Allowed types | ext `.jpg .jpeg .png .pdf .doc .docx` AND matching MIME | `checkFileType`, `upload.route.js:12-27` |
| Max size | 15 MB | `limits: { fileSize: 15 * 1024 * 1024 }` |
| Storage | Cloudinary (memory buffer → `upload_stream`) | `upload.service.js:23-46` |
| Success response | `{ url, public_id, resource_type }` | `upload.service.js:42-46` |
| Backend port | `3000` | `.env` → `PORT=3000` |
| Frontend sends token? | **No** — `uploadFile()` sends no `Authorization` header | `JobLoom-App-SSD-main/src/services/uploadApi.js:22-26` |

## Prerequisites
1. Backend running: `cd JobLoom-BE-SSD-main && npm run dev`
2. Seed account exists: `npm run seed:basic`
3. **One manual step:** in request `03` and `02`, the `file` form field must point at `postman/test-files/upload-test.png`. See the guide — set Postman's working directory to that folder, or click **Select File** once per request.

## Run order
`00` → `01` → `02` → `03` → `04` → `05`

## How to read the result
| Request 03 outcome | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Test **fails** with 200 + file URL | `VULNERABLE: File upload succeeded without authentication.` |
| Test **passes** with 401/403 | `PROTECTED: Authentication was required.` |
| `INCONCLUSIVE` in console | Usually the test file was not selected — fix and re-run |

## Purpose — CONTROL, not the attack
Establishes that the upload endpoint works normally for an authenticated employer. Without this baseline, a failure in request `03` could be blamed on a broken endpoint.

## Request
- Method: **POST**
- URL: `{{baseUrl}}/api/upload`
- Body: **multipart/form-data**
  - `file` → `upload-test.png` (file)
  - `folder` → `{{uploadFolder}}` (text, optional)
- Auth: **Bearer `{{authToken}}`** (from request 01)

## Expected
| Check | Value |
| --- | --- |
| HTTP | **200** |
| Body | `{ "url": "https://res.cloudinary.com/...", "public_id": "...", "resource_type": "image" }` |

## Automated
Saves `url` → `baselineFileUrl`, `public_id` → `baselinePublicId`.

## If you get 400 "No file uploaded"
The file row is not attached. Select `postman/test-files/upload-test.png` in the Body tab (see the guide).

request.description:
## THIS IS THE VULNERABILITY TEST
Byte-for-byte the same request as `02`, with **all credentials removed**.

| Aspect | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Method / URL | `POST {{baseUrl}}/api/upload` |
| Authorization tab | **No Auth** (explicitly set — nothing inherited) |
| Bearer token | none |
| Saved login token | not referenced anywhere in this request |
| Auth cookie | none added by this collection |
| Body | same `file` + `folder` multipart fields |

The collection root is also set to **No Auth**, so there is nothing to inherit.

## Verdict logic (decided at runtime, never hard-coded)
| Actual response | Verdict printed |
| --- | --- |
| 2xx **and** body has a valid `url` | `VULNERABLE: File upload succeeded without authentication.` |
| **401 or 403** | `PROTECTED: Authentication was required.` |
| anything else (e.g. 400 no file, 502 provider error) | `INCONCLUSIVE` + the likely cause |

## Test results you will see
- `CONCLUSION → VULNERABLE` / `PROTECTED` / `INCONCLUSIVE` — informational, always passes
- `Endpoint should reject unauthenticated upload with 401/403` — **fails if vulnerable**, passes if protected

## Automated
On a successful unauthenticated upload: saves `url` → `uploadedFileUrl`, `public_id` → `uploadedPublicId` for request `04`.

## Note on 502
A 502 means the request got past the route into the Cloudinary call — i.e. it was **not** rejected for missing authentication. Fix `CLOUDINARY_*` in `.env` and re-run for clean evidence.

request.description:
## Purpose
Proves the upload was actually **persisted**, completing the chain:

`Upload accepted` → `File stored` → `Returned file accessible`

## Why the URL bar looks empty before you run 03
This request's address is `{{uploadedFileUrl}}`. That variable starts blank on purpose. Request `03` fills it. The pre-request script then writes the real Cloudinary URL onto this GET.

**Do this:** send `03` first (must return a `url`), then send `04`. Do not skip 03.

If `03` did not save a URL, `04` falls back to `{{baselineFileUrl}}` from request `02` so the request is not empty.

## Outcomes
| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **200** + image content-type | File is stored **and** publicly retrievable — strongest evidence |
| **401 / 403** | File was stored, but the provider restricts direct delivery. Persistence is still proven by the `public_id` from request 03. |
| Pre-request error "No file URL yet" | You opened 04 before 02/03 saved a URL. Run 03, then 04. |

## Scope
Read-only GET of your own harmless test image. **No attempt is made to bypass any storage-provider access control.**

console.log('[05] So a 401 here + a 200 in request 03 shows the omission is specific to POST, not a server-wide lack of auth.');

request.description:
## Purpose — corroborating control
The **same router file** (`src/routes/upload.route.js`) protects its GET route but not its POST route:
- line 64: `router.get('/signed-url', protect, ...)` ✅ protected
- line 111: `router.post('/', cloudUpload.single('file'), ...)` ❌ no auth

## Expected
HTTP **401** `{"message":"Not authorized, no token"}`

## Why it strengthens the finding
A 401 here proves authentication middleware is present and working in this module. Combined with a 200 from request `03`, it shows the POST endpoint's missing `protect` is a specific defect — not a misconfigured server or a disabled auth system.

## Not an attack
This is a plain unauthenticated GET expected to be refused. No bypass is attempted.
